Search this repository (/bench/home/work) for any per-user API rate-limiting middleware. I need to know:
1. Does such middleware exist at all?
2. If it exists, where is it registered/wired up (file path, line number)?
3. What are its configured request limits (e.g., requests per minute/second, per user)?

Search broadly: grep for terms like "rateLimit", "rate-limit", "rate_limit", "throttle", "RateLimiter", "express-rate-limit", "limiter", "requestsPerMinute", "quota", etc. Check middleware directories, server setup files, config files, and any API gateway configs. Also check package.json for rate-limiting libraries (express-rate-limit, rate-limiter-flexible, etc.).

Report back concisely: whether it exists, and if so exact file paths and limit values. If it does NOT exist, say so clearly and note what related things (if any) do exist (e.g. any other kind of throttling, unrelated middleware, etc.) so I can give an accurate premise correction to the user.

Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
## Findings

**1. Does per-user API rate-limiting middleware exist? No.**

I searched broadly across the whole repo (this is the Go/TS "memos" project) for `rateLimit`, `rate-limit`, `rate_limit`, `throttle`, `RateLimiter`, `express-rate-limit`, `limiter`, `quota`, `requestsPerMinute`, and `golang.org/x/time/rate`. There is no rate-limiting middleware or interceptor anywhere in the codebase, and no rate-limiting library in either `go.mod`/`go.sum` or `web/package.json`.

**2. Where middleware/interceptors ARE registered (for context):**

The actual request-processing chain is in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-141`, which wires up the Connect-RPC interceptor chain:

```go
connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
    NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
    NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
)
```

Implementations are in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`:
- `MetadataInterceptor` — copies HTTP headers (User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For, Origin, Cookie, etc.) into gRPC metadata and sets no-cache response headers.
- `LoggingInterceptor` — logs requests/errors.
- `RecoveryInterceptor` — recovers panics, converts to `connect.CodeInternal`.
- `AuthInterceptor` — authenticates and checks access via `Authorizer`.

None of these throttle or limit request rate per user, per IP, or globally.

**3. Configured limits: none exist.** There are no requests-per-minute/second values, no token-bucket configs, no per-user quotas anywhere.

**What DOES exist (related but not rate-limiting), for an accurate premise correction:**

- **Request body size limit** (not a rate limit) at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`: `const maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20` (256 MiB), applied via `http.MaxBytesHandler` and `connect.WithReadMaxBytes`. This caps payload size, not request frequency.
- **`/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/middleware.go`** — this is a false-positive style match; it's middleware for the *background job scheduler* (Recovery, Logging, Timeout for scheduled jobs), completely unrelated to HTTP API request rate-limiting.
- **`/bench/home/work/internal/email/doc.go:86`** — one doc comment says "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" as a *suggested* security consideration in the SMTP package's documentation, but there is no actual implementation of it anywhere — it's just a recommendation in a comment, not real code.
- No `nginx.conf` or reverse-proxy config exists in the repo (only `scripts/Dockerfile`), so there's no gateway-level rate limiting configured in-repo either (any such limiting would have to be added by whoever deploys the container, e.g., via an external reverse proxy).
- No login-attempt lockout/brute-force protection was found in `server/auth/` or the auth session service either — only a doc comment about "suspicious login attempts" (`server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:277`), again with no accompanying implementation.

**Bottom line:** There is currently no per-user (or any other kind of) API rate-limiting middleware in this codebase. If the user believed one existed, that premise is incorrect — the only "rate limit" references in the repo are aspirational comments, not working code.
